There may also be an economic impact generated from livestock and crop depredations by animals that are endangered.
On occasion, construction of roads and highways and large airports may destroy endangered species habitat or compromise its ability to produce and sustain endangered animals.
A number of animals are particularly susceptible to the toxic effects of certain pesticides used in the environment. Particularly vulnerable are the birds at or near the top of the biological food chain where they accumulate high concentrations of pesticides picked up by their prey.

Some of these bird species are endangered as a result. Curtailment of the use of harmful pesticides will be necessary for the restoration of these endangered species or substitute methods of pest control will have to be developed.
Twenty-five species and subspecies listed in the "Red Book" are suffering from crowding by the expanding human population of the United States. Some endangered animals live close to urban and industrial areas. The demand for new housing and commercial sites has lead to the overrun of small habitats, often aquatic, that harbored an isolated endangered animal. More such habitat sites lie in the path of our expanding population and must be protected if we are to successfully restore the endangered species involved.
